`verus /work/ringbuffer_dequeue.rs` now prints `verification results:: 6 verified, 0 errors`. Verus also prints a trigger-selection note for the `assert forall` in the proof, which is only a note.

The body of `dequeue` is in the `// <code>` block:
- It reads `self.data[self.head]` as the return value.
- It advances `self.head` by one, wrapping to 0 when it reaches `capacity`.
- It decrements `self.len`.

That is O(1); no elements are shifted.

The proof is inside the function body, so the `// <helpers>` and `// <proofs>` regions are unchanged. Three steps carry it:
- The returned value equals `old(self).view()[0]` once `head % capacity == head`, which follows from `head < capacity`.
- The new `head` equals `(head + 1) % capacity`.
- Element `i` of the new view equals element `i` of `old(self).view().drop_first()`. This uses `lemma_add_mod_noop` and `lemma_mod_twice` from vstd.
